mainTopic: The young heir who may not yet sell his father's land: when he counts as an adult, what proves he understands, and whether his testimony and gifts are valid
overview: The גמרא continues asking whether a young heir may sell his late father's land from age 18 or only from age 20. It first defends the age 20 view: a משנה in נדה about a סריס applies only when he shows סריס signs. Someone without those signs stays a minor until 'most of his years,' as רבי חייא teaches. Next the גמרא asks whether the year of coming of age counts as before or after that age, and gets two reports of רב נחמן's view. It explains that רבא's version was only inferred from a case where the seller was plainly foolish. רבא then rules that a fourteen-year-old girl who understands business can buy and sell. A story about a young seller, date pits and a clever remark ends with רבא upholding the sale, because he understands when things are explained to him. Finally, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע and מר זוטרא discuss whether such a young heir can testify, and אמימר rules that his gift is valid. רב אשי challenges אמימר, and אמימר's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why examine the body if adulthood starts at twenty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes saying that the 18 view explains why the relatives wanted to examine the body. It then asks what such an exam could do under the 20 view.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why they came and asked רבי עקיבא, 'May we examine him?' But if you say a young heir may sell only from age twenty, what would examining him accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a sentence from the previous lines and turns it into a challenge against the view that a young heir may sell only from age 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the age 18 view, a body exam could show whether the seller was an adult, so asking makes sense. Under the age 20 view, it seems an exam would change nothing. Step 2 will bring a משנה to show why.

keyTerms.meaning: this is (why) — the explanation for something
to examine him (here, the dead man's body for signs of adulthood)
but if you say — sets up a challenge against a view
what would it accomplish? / what difference does it make?

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of a sentence. The opening words 'הַיְינוּ דְּקָאָתוּ' finish an earlier 'בשלמא' line: under the age 18 view, the relatives' question makes sense.

phrases.english: this is why they came and said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי עקיבא. This line finishes a thought from before: under the age 18 view, their question makes sense.

phrases.english: What is the law — may we examine him?
phrases.notes: They wanted to check the dead seller's body for signs that he had already become an adult.

phrases.english: But if you say from age twenty,
when they examine him, what would it accomplish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the 'granted for age 18' line from before this text and turns it against the age 20 view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a young heir may sell his father's land only from age 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the age 20 view, a body exam seems pointless, so the relatives' question to רבי עקיבא would make no sense.

steps.title: The משנה about a twenty-year-old without signs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a משנה: a 20-year-old without two hairs is treated as a סריס once his age is proven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we learn in a משנה: If a twenty-year-old has not grown two hairs, they bring proof that he is twenty, and he is the סריס. He does neither חליצה nor יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to show why examining a 20-year-old's body seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to say that once someone is proven to be 20, his age decides his status, not signs on his body. If so, an exam adds nothing under the age 20 view. That makes the challenge from Step 1 stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn (in a משנה)?
two hairs — the physical sign of reaching adulthood
a man who never develops physically
does חליצה / does יבום (the rules for a brother's childless widow)

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת
phrases.english: A twenty-year-old who did not grow two hairs
they should bring proof that he is twenty;
and he is the sexually underdeveloped man,
he neither performs halitza nor levirate marriage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the challenge in Step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That at age 20 a body exam would make no difference.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נדה: a 20-year-old without two hairs, once his age is proven, is a סריס.

steps.title: The משנה applies only when he shows signs of a סריס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers using רב's limit on the משנה: it applies only when the man has the physical signs of a סריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about that משנה, in the name of רב: this is only when signs of a סריס developed in him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting the משנה to someone who actually shows the signs of a סריס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 20 alone does not make someone without two hairs an adult or a סריס. He also needs the physical signs of a סריס. So under the age 20 view, a body exam still matters: it can show whether those signs were there.

keyTerms.meaning: wasn't it said about it? — brings a known statement on that source
the physical signs of a סריס
developed in him / appeared on him

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the age 20 view, and it sets the rule that age alone, without the סריס signs, does not decide adulthood.

phrases.english: Wasn't it said about it:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said in the name of Rav:
and that is only when signs of a sexually underdeveloped man developed in him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the משנה quoted in Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the source (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any proven 20-year-old without two hairs counts as a סריס, so an exam is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone who also shows סריס signs counts as one, so an exam still matters at 20.

steps.title: רבא shows the wording of the משנה supports this
steps.stepSummary: רבא points to the words 'he is THE סריס' as proof that the משנה means someone clearly marked as a סריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The wording is exact too, because it says 'and he is THE סריס.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up רב's limit from Step 3 by pointing to the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'הוּא הַסָּרִיס' ('he is THE סריס') point to a person known as a סריס, someone with the signs. The גמרא accepts this with 'שמע מינה.'

keyTerms.meaning: it is also exact — the wording itself supports this
since it teaches / because it says
learn from it — the point is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: The age 20 view stands. A 20-year-old without two hairs is a סריס only if he has the סריס signs, so examining a body can still make a difference.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is also precise,
since it teaches: 'and he is THE sexually underdeveloped man';
phrases.notes: The word 'the' points to someone clearly known as a סריס, because he has the signs.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 3 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב's limit: the משנה applies only when סריס signs are present.

steps.title: Without סריס signs, how long is he a minor?
steps.stepSummary: If he never grows two hairs and has no סריס signs, until what age is he treated as a minor?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if no signs of a סריס appeared on him, until how long is he a minor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question that comes out of the answer in Step 3, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 taught that age 20 alone does not make him an adult when he has no סריס signs. So there must be some later point when he finally counts as an adult. The גמרא asks when that is.

keyTerms.meaning: and if not / and when it is not so
until how long?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לָא נוֹלְדוּ לוֹ סִימָנֵי סָרִיס,
phrases.english: And if signs of a sexually underdeveloped man did not develop in him,
until when is he a minor?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לָא נוֹלְדוּ לוֹ סִימָנֵי סָרִיס, עַד כַּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the limit set in Step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age at which someone with no hairs and no סריס signs finally counts as an adult.

steps.title: רבי חייא: until most of his years
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that he stays a minor until most of his years have passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: Until most of his years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5 with a teaching of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Most of his years' means most of a normal lifetime. Only after that point is he treated as an adult even though he never showed the signs.

keyTerms.meaning: most of his years — more than half of a normal lifespan

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya taught:
Until most of his years.
phrases.notes: Most of a seventy-year life, so until about age 35.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He stays a minor until most of his years have passed.

steps.title: רבי חייא's advice: change his body weight
steps.stepSummary: In practice, רבי חייא would tell people to make a thin person fatter or a fat person thinner, since the signs can come from either.
steps.simpleTranslation: When such a case came before רבי חייא: if the person was thin, he told them, 'Let him get fat.' If he was fat, he told them, 'Let him get thin.' These signs sometimes come because of thinness, and sometimes because of fatness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how רבי חייא actually handled people who had not grown the signs: he tried to help the signs appear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before he declares someone a סריס, רבי חייא tries changing his body condition, since the signs can be held back by being too thin or too fat. This shows the signs may still come later. That is why he is not quickly labeled a סריס.

keyTerms.meaning: thin, lean
let him become fat / healthy
let him become thin
sometimes

phrases.english: When such a case came before Rabbi Chiyya,
phrases.notes: The case of a person who had not grown the two hairs.

phrases.english: if he was thin, he would say to them: Let him become fat;
and if he was fat, he would say to them: Let him become thin.
because these signs
sometimes come because of thinness,
sometimes come because of fatness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי חייא's practical approach to his rule in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before ruling on someone without signs, try making him fatter or thinner, since the signs can depend on body condition.
steps.whatToRemember: Someone without hairs and without סריס signs stays a minor until most of his years. Meanwhile, רבי חייא tried to help the signs appear by changing his weight.

steps.title: Does the year itself count as before or after?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: during the year when he reaches the selling age, is he treated as before that age or after it?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is 'during the time' treated like 'before the time' or like 'after the time'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the selling age, setting up two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heir comes of age for selling 'in' a certain year (his 18th or 20th). The question is whether that whole year still counts as before he comes of age, or already as after. The difference is whether a sale during that year is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: they asked / a question was raised among the חכמים
during the time — within the year of coming of age
before the time / after the time

steps.confusionAlert: 'Time' here is not a moment. It means the whole year in which he reaches the selling age, and the question is how to treat that entire year.

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
Is 'during the time' like 'before the time,'
phrases.notes: The 'time' is the year he reaches the selling age, his 18th or 20th.

phrases.english: or like 'after the time'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the selling age itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the year of coming of age counts as before or after reaching that age.

steps.title: רבא quoting רב נחמן: like before
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that רב נחמן said the year itself is treated like before the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: 'During the time' is like 'before the time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer to the question: the year still counts as before he comes of age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this version, he is not yet old enough to sell until the whole year has passed. A sale during that year would not be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: like before the time — still not of age

phrases.english: Rava said in the name of Rav Nachman:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word 'אמר' in round brackets.

phrases.english: 'During the time' is like 'before the time.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives one answer to the question in Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The year of coming of age counts as before the time, so he cannot sell yet.

steps.title: רבא בר רב שילא quoting רב נחמן: like after
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב שילא reports the opposite in רב נחמן's name: the year itself is treated like after the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב שילא said in the name of רב נחמן: 'During the time' is like 'after the time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, opposite report of what רב נחמן held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this version, once he enters that year he already counts as of age, so a sale during the year is valid. The argument is about what רב נחמן actually said, not a new opinion of a different teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: like after the time — already of age

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions quote the same רב נחמן. The two students disagree about what he said, not about their own views.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Sheila said in the name of Rav Nachman:
'During the time' is like 'after the time.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a report of רב נחמן's view that is the opposite of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The year of coming of age counts as after the time, so he may already sell during it.

steps.title: רבא's ruling was only an inference from a case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ruling in רבא's name (the year itself is like before the time) was never said outright. People inferred it from a case where רבא cancelled a sale made during that year.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ruling of רבא was not said outright. It was inferred. Someone in 'the year itself' sold property. The case came to רבא, and he said the sale was worthless. Whoever saw this assumed the reason was that the year itself counts like before the time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the report in step 9 and explains where it really came from: a case, not a direct statement. This step sets up the next move, where the גמרא will show that the inference was mistaken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 reported that רבא quoted רב נחמן as saying the year itself is like before the time. Now we learn that nobody heard רבא say this. Onlookers only saw him cancel a sale made in that year and guessed his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Said outright, in so many words
By inference, worked out from a case
During the time: the year itself in which he reaches the age
He did nothing at all; the act has no effect

phrases.english: And this ruling of Rava
phrases.notes: This points back to the report in רבא's name that the year itself counts like before the time.

phrases.english: was not stated explicitly
rather, it was stated by inference
for there was a certain person within the time
who went and sold property
and it came before Rava

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְלוּם.
phrases.english: He said to them: He did not do anything.
Whoever saw it assumed
that it was because within the time is like before the time

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרָבָא, לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִיתְּמַר, אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains where the report in step 9 came from, which weakens it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling that the year itself is like before the time was only inferred from רבא cancelling a sale made in that year.

steps.title: The inference was wrong because the seller acted foolishly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. רבא cancelled the sale because the seller showed clear foolishness: he was freeing his slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There, רבא saw extra foolishness in him, because he was freeing his slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the onlookers misread רבא's reason. The sale was cancelled because of the seller's foolish behavior, not because of his age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Freeing one's slaves for no reason showed that this person could not manage property. So רבא's ruling was about this one foolish seller. It teaches nothing about the year itself, and the report in step 9 loses its support.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so: a rejection of what was just said
Extra, obvious foolishness
Freeing (slaves)

steps.whatToRemember: A ruling based on one person's foolish behavior cannot be turned into a general rule about age.

phrases.english: But it is not so
there, he saw excessive foolishness in him
for he was freeing his slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, הָתָם שְׁטוּתָא יַתִּירְתָא חֲזָא בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference described in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבא held the year itself is like before the time.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The onlookers missed the real reason: the seller's obvious foolishness in freeing his slaves.

steps.title: גידל בר מנשיא asks about a fourteen-year-old girl
steps.stepSummary: גידל בר מנשיא writes to רבא about a girl of fourteen years and one day who understands business. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: גידל בר מנשיא sent to רבא: 'Let our teacher teach us. A girl of fourteen years and one day understands business. What is the law?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new question starts here. גידל בר מנשיא asks whether a young girl who understands business can buy and sell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question focuses on two facts: her exact age and her understanding of business. He wants to know whether that understanding is enough to make her deals valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Let our teacher teach us: a polite opening for a question
A young girl
The way business dealings work

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ גִּידֵּל בַּר מְנַשְּׁיָא לְרָבָא,
phrases.english: Giddel bar Menashya sent to Rava:
Let our teacher instruct us:

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹקֶת בַּת אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: A girl fourteen years and one day old
who understands the nature of business dealings; what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ גִּידֵּל בַּר מְנַשְּׁיָא לְרָבָא, יְלַמְּדֵנוּ רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about young sellers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a fourteen-year-old girl who understands business can make a valid purchase or sale.

steps.title: רבא answers that her deals are valid
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that if she understands business, her purchase is a purchase and her sale is a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא sent back: 'If she understands business, what she buys is bought and what she sells is sold.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. Understanding business is what makes her deals count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not rest his answer on her age alone. The deciding factor is whether she understands business. If she does, her deals are fully valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Her purchase is a valid purchase
Her sale is a valid sale

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer is the ruling that the young seller in step 19 later relied on.

phrases.english: He sent to him:
If she understands the nature of business dealings
her purchase is a purchase and her sale is a sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ: אִם יוֹדַעַת בְּטִיב מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If she understands business, her purchases and sales are valid.

steps.title: Why not ask about a boy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why גידל asked about a girl. He could have asked about a boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him ask about a boy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how the question was worded. Why was it about a girl and not a boy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every detail in a question is chosen on purpose. So it wants to know why the question was framed around a girl.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him send (ask) him instead
A young boy

phrases.english: But let him send to him about a boy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of a girl in גידל's question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the question is about young sellers, asking about a boy would have seemed the more obvious choice.

steps.title: That is how the case happened
steps.stepSummary: The answer: that is how the real case happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case that happened, happened this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the question was about a real event, and in that event the seller was a girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail does not teach a special law about girls. It just reflects the facts of the real case.

keyTerms.meaning: The case that happened, happened this way

phrases.english: The incident that happened, happened this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual: the detail comes from a real case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Choosing a girl was meant to teach something special.
steps.terutzMaskana: The detail simply matches the real event.

steps.title: Why not ask about a twelve-year-old girl
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the girl in the question was fourteen. He could have asked about a girl of twelve years and one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him ask about a girl of twelve years and one day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges another detail in the question: why fourteen and not twelve?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twelve years and one day is a well-known age for a girl, so the גמרא wonders why the question names fourteen. It again assumes the detail was chosen on purpose.

keyTerms.term: בַּת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד
keyTerms.meaning: A girl of twelve years and one day

phrases.english: But let him send to him

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹקֶת בַּת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד!
phrases.english: about a girl twelve years and one day old!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִישְׁלַח לֵיהּ תִּינוֹקֶת בַּת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the wording of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The age of fourteen in the question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Twelve years and one day is the known age for a girl, so why name fourteen?

steps.title: Again, that is how the case happened
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: that is how the real case happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case that happened, happened this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer: in the real case, the girl was fourteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The age of fourteen is just a fact of the real event. It is not a new legal age limit.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's answer to גידל depends on understanding business. The details about a girl of fourteen come from a real event.

phrases.english: The incident that happened, happened this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual: the detail comes from a real case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The age of fourteen was meant to teach something.
steps.terutzMaskana: The age simply matches the real event.

steps.title: Another ruling of רבא was only an inference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says another ruling of רבא was also only inferred from a case. Someone under twenty sold his father's property, relying on רבא's answer to גידל בר מנשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ruling of רבא was also not said outright. It was inferred. Someone under twenty went and sold his father's property, relying on the ruling given to גידל בר מנשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case of a ruling that was only inferred. It sets up the scene: a young man under twenty sold his father's property, relying on רבא's answer in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller understood business, so he expected his sale to count, just as רבא told גידל. The result of the case comes in the next step. This step sets the stage for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Younger than twenty
His father's property

phrases.english: And this ruling of Rava
was not stated explicitly
rather, it was stated by inference
for there was a certain person under twenty
who went and sold his father's property
in line with Giddel bar Menashya.
phrases.notes: He means: relying on the answer רבא sent to גידל, that understanding business makes a sale valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרָבָא, לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִיתְּמַר, אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's answer in step 14 with a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ruling of רבא about a seller under twenty came only from a case, not from a direct statement.

steps.title: The date-pit test and רבא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The seller's relatives told him to eat dates and throw the pits into רבא's house. He did, and רבא ruled that his sale was invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case came before רבא. The relatives told the young man: 'Go eat dates and throw the pits into רבא's house.' He did it, and רבא said: 'His sale is not a sale.'
steps.whatsHappening: The relatives got the young man to show his foolishness in front of רבא. רבא then cancelled the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For now, רבא cancels the sale because the seller seems to act foolishly, not simply because he is under twenty. The story continues, and in steps 21–24 רבא changes his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: His relatives
Dates
Pits (of the dates)
His sale is not a valid sale

steps.confusionAlert: Do not learn from this case that anyone under twenty can never sell. רבא cancelled the sale because the seller showed foolishness, just like the slave-freeing case in step 12.
steps.whatToRemember: This ruling is not the end of the story. In step 22 רבא reverses it and upholds the sale.

phrases.english: It came before Rava.
His relatives said to him:
Go eat dates
and throw the pits into Rava's house.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: He did so.
He said to them: His sale is not a sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ קְרוֹבֵיהּ: זִיל אֱכוֹל תַּמְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case begun in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא first cancels the sale because the seller seems foolish. This ruling is reversed in step 22.

steps.title: The buyers coach the young man to say something clever
steps.stepSummary: While רבא's ruling was being written, the buyers had the young man make a sharp remark about the price of the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: While they were writing up the ruling for him, the buyers told him: Go tell רבא, 'A whole מגילת אסתר costs one זוז, and the Master's little document costs one זוז too?!' He went and said it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going. The buyers want to show רבא that the young man is actually sharp, so they give him a clever line to say. This sets up רבא's next ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had just cancelled the sale because the young man seemed foolish (step 20). The buyers answer that with a test. If he can deliver a sharp, witty complaint, he is not really lacking in understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: A written document; here, the document recording רבא's ruling
Buyers; the people who bought the property from the young man
A zuz, a silver coin
The scroll of Esther, a long written scroll

phrases.english: When they were writing the document for him,
phrases.notes: This is the document with רבא's ruling that the sale was invalid.

phrases.english: the buyers said to him:
Go and say to רבא:
A מגילת אסתר costs a zuz;
and the Master's document costs a zuz too?!
phrases.notes: He is complaining that a short ruling cost as much as a whole long scroll. That is a clever point to make.

phrases.english: He went and said it to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after רבא cancelled the sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The buyers set up a test to show that the young man is sharp.

steps.title: רבא now rules that the sale is valid
steps.stepSummary: After hearing the clever remark, רבא reverses himself and upholds the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to them: His sale is a valid sale.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא hears the sharp remark and changes his ruling: the sale stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבא saw only foolish behavior and cancelled the sale. Now he sees that the young man can think sharply, so he treats him as someone whose sale counts.

keyTerms.meaning: His sale is a sale; the sale is valid

phrases.english: He said to them: His sale is a valid sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא's reaction to the remark in step 21; it reverses his ruling in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The young man's sale is valid.

steps.title: The relatives object that the buyers coached him
steps.stepSummary: The relatives argue that the clever remark proves nothing, because the buyers taught it to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: His relatives said to רבא: The buyers taught him to say that!
steps.whatsHappening: The young man's relatives push back against רבא's new ruling. They say the clever line wasn't really his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The relatives want the sale cancelled so the property stays in the family. Their claim is that a memorized line does not show real understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: His relatives
They taught him; they coached him

phrases.english: His relatives said to him:
The buyers taught him that!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the sale is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A line someone else prepared for him does not prove that he understands anything.

steps.title: רבא: if he understands when things are explained, he knows what he is doing
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that being able to understand an explanation is enough. The date-pit episode was חוצפה, not foolishness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When they explain something to him, he understands it. Since he understands when things are explained, he knows what he is doing. And what he did before was just extra חוצפה in him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the relatives. Even if the buyers coached him, he understood the point and could deliver it. So he knows what he is doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is not whether he came up with the idea himself. The test is whether he understands when someone explains something to him. Throwing pits into רבא's house is then explained as rudeness, not a lack of understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: They explain it to him
He understands
Extra חוצפה, excessive rudeness

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling in the story: the sale stands. This is the case that the ruling in רבא's name (step 19) was inferred from: someone under twenty who understands when things are explained to him knows what he is doing, so his sale is valid. Odd behavior can just be חוצפה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not deny that the buyers coached him. His point is that understanding an explanation is already enough.

phrases.english: He said to them: When they explain it to him, he understands.
Since when they explain to him he understands,
he certainly knows what he is doing,
and the fact that he acted this way
phrases.notes: He means throwing the date pits into רבא's house from step 20.

phrases.english: was just extra חוצפה that was in him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the relatives' objection in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what counts as proof of understanding
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a remark he thought of himself would prove he understands.
steps.terutzMaskana: Understanding an explanation is enough. The strange behavior was חוצפה, so the sale stands.

steps.title: The under-twenty heir's testimony is valid
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rules that the young man who cannot yet sell his father's land can still serve as a witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: As for testimony, his testimony is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from selling to a new question about the same young man: can he be a witness? רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young man is not trusted to sell his father's land, but that does not automatically disqualify him as a witness. Not being allowed to sell does not mean he lacks understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said:
And as for testimony, his testimony is valid testimony.
phrases.notes: He means the young man who is not yet old enough to sell land he inherited from his father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וּלְעֵדוּת – עֵדוּתוֹ עֵדוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the same young man: testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The under-twenty heir's testimony is valid.

steps.title: מר זוטרא limits it to movable property
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the young man's testimony counts only for movable things, not for land.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: We said his testimony is valid only for movable property, but not for land.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא narrows the ruling just given. The young man can testify about movable items but not about land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This limit parallels selling: the young man can sell movable things but not his father's land. מר זוטרא ties the right to testify to the right to sell.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable property
Land, real estate
We only said this about...

phrases.english: מר זוטרא said:
We said this only about movable property,
but about land, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא לְמִטַּלְטְלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's ruling from step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His testimony is valid for movable property but not for land.

steps.title: רב אשי: by that logic, little children could testify
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that if the ability to sell makes testimony valid, then פעוטות, who can sell movables, should be valid witnesses too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to מר זוטרא: Why are movables different? Because his sale of movables is valid? If so, the משנה says that young children's purchases and sales of movables are valid. Would their testimony also be valid?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges מר זוטרא's reasoning. He shows that it would lead to an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא seems to link testifying to selling. But young children can also buy and sell movables, and everyone knows children cannot be witnesses. So the ability to sell cannot be the reason testimony is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
But if so... (introduces an impossible result)
Young children
Buying and selling

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא:
phrases.english: רב אשי said to מר זוטרא:
Why are movables different?
Because his sale of them is valid?
But if so, what about what we learned in a משנה:
Young children: their purchase is a valid purchase
and their sale is a valid sale, for movable property.
Would their testimony also be valid testimony?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא: מַאי שְׁנָא מִטַּלְטְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind מר זוטרא's limit in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's link between valid sales and valid testimony
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Young children can sell movables but certainly cannot testify. So being able to sell cannot make someone a valid witness.

steps.title: Children are different because witnesses must be 'men'
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that testimony has its own requirement from the פסוק, that witnesses be men, and children do not meet it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, I need 'and the two men shall stand,' and that is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא explains why children are left out. The תורה requires witnesses to be 'men,' and young children are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children are disqualified by a separate rule from the פסוק, not by the question of whether they can sell. The under-twenty heir is an adult man, so that rule does not block him.

keyTerms.meaning: I require
'And the two men shall stand'; the source that witnesses must be men
And it is missing

phrases.english: He said to him: There, with children,
I need 'and the two men shall stand,'
and that is missing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם, בָּעֵינָא וְעָמְדוּ שְׁנֵי הָאֲנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a separate disqualification that applies only to children
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If ability to sell made testimony valid, children could testify about movables.
steps.terutzMaskana: Children are disqualified because witnesses must be 'men.' The adult heir is not affected by that rule.

steps.title: אמימר: the young heir's gift is valid
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that even though the young man cannot sell his father's land, a gift he gives is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: And his gift is a valid gift.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds a ruling about the same young man. If he gives a gift, it counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a third area after selling and testifying. אמימר treats giving a gift differently from selling.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift

phrases.english: אמימר said:
And his gift is a valid gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about the same young man, this time about gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The under-twenty heir's gift is valid.

steps.title: רב אשי: a gift should be even worse than a sale
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues with a קל וחומר: if a sale, where he gets money, is invalid, a gift, where he gets nothing, should certainly be invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: Now, a sale, where he gets money, you say is not valid, because he might sell too cheaply. All the more so a gift, where he gets nothing at all!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר using a קל וחומר, an 'all the more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young man cannot sell because he might sell too cheaply and lose value. With a gift he loses everything and gets nothing back. So the worry should be even bigger, and a gift should certainly be invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (opens an 'all the more so' argument)
He sells cheaply, for too low a price
All the more so

phrases.english: רב אשי said to אמימר:
Now, if a sale,
where he receives money,
you say is not valid,
because he might sell it too cheaply;
then all the more so a gift,
where nothing at all comes to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר: הַשְׁתָּא, וּמָה זְבִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that the young heir's gift is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the reason for blocking sales, losing value, applies even more strongly to a gift.

steps.title: אמימר begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: אמימר starts to answer רב אשי. His answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up אמימר's reply to the קל וחומר. The actual answer comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, all we know is that אמימר does not accept רב אשי's challenge. He will explain why a gift is different from a sale.

phrases.english: He said to him:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens אמימר's answer to רב אשי's challenge in step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A gift should be even less valid than a sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated on this amud; it comes at the start of the next amud.
